cases.quote: The character width of hyphens (cl-03) varies according to the type of hyphen. HYPHEN "‐" should be quarter em width (i.e. one quarter of an em width), EN DASH "–" and KATAKANA-HIRAGANA DOUBLE HYPHEN "゠" should be half-width (a half em width), WAVE DASH "〜" should be full-width. Basically there should be no spacing before and after hyphens (cl-03). However, half em spacing should be appended, in principle, when opening brackets (cl-01) follow right after a hyphen (cl-03) and quarter em spacing when middle dots (cl-05) follow a hyphen (cl-03).

This paragraph's own final sentence is Table 1's own cl-03 row read in prose, and this case pins its first clause: `table1.rs`'s cell at cl-03 before cl-01 — `(3, 1)` — carries one term, `trailing: true, amount: em(360)`, i.e. `Referent::Trailing`, owned by the opening bracket that follows the hyphen rather than by the hyphen itself, exactly as the quoted sentence's own word order states it ("half em spacing... when opening brackets... follow right after a hyphen" names the bracket's own trailing contribution, not the hyphen's). §3.1.6's own fourth Note (not quoted above, quoted in full by `3.1.6/closing-bracket-then-ideograph/the-brackets-own-half-em`'s own rationale) is what licenses crediting this rule's own address for a cell Appendix B's bare opening sentence also states. `table3.rs`'s own cell at this coordinate states `limit: Some(em(0)), stage: 5` — the identical fifth-priority drain-to-solid the closing-bracket case above reads at a different pair, read directly from the generated cell rather than assumed. The hyphen's own declared frame — quarter em, `advance: 250` on this case's 1000-unit scale — follows the paragraph's own first sentence and matches `A.3/hyphen/on-the-quarter-em-frame`'s own classify case, though classifying the hyphen is that case's province and not reasserted here; this case's own assertion is the amount at the boundary, not the class of either item.
